set.approach: The Island is a granite plug rising directly above the Cody climbers parking area. Drive west from Cody through Shoshone Canyon on Highway 14/16, pass the two short tunnels, and park at the pull-in on the highway's north side ahead of the long tunnel. The route follows the featured crack on the northwest face of the Island, reached by going over the hill on the Green Mile approach and down the trail, then turning sharply left to a belay platform beneath the scree field.

review.notes: Island page: parking; route page: northwest face and approach. No descent stated.

set.approach: The Island is a granite plug rising directly above the Cody climbers parking area, reached by driving west from Cody through Shoshone Canyon on Highway 14/16 and parking at the pull-in on the highway's north side ahead of the long tunnel. The route takes the Island's south arete, left of Jesus Loves You and near the parking lot, and begins on a wide hand-and-fist crack.

review.notes: MP search first hit South Ridge of the South Teton (wrong); the right page is the Cody Island one, breadcrumb Wyoming > Cody > The Island Area > The Island. No descent stated.

set.approach: Little Seneca Lake lies on the way from the Elkhart Park trailhead (Pole Creek trail) toward Island Lake and Gannett Peak. The route is on the north side of the lake, a few yards from the water. Follow the trail along the west shore round to the north side, pass the black-streaked rock on your left, leave the trail toward the shore at the first opportunity, continue past Gymnast In My Duffle Bag and around a rock outcrop. The first big crack system past the outcrop, on its east side, is the route.
set.descent_text: Walk off easily to climber's left, or rappel from trees above the route.

review.notes: Route page gives both the location and the descent.

set.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. The A-Frame Buttress, which looks like its name, stands on climber's right at the entrance to the cirque; the route follows its obvious crack system.
set.descent_text: Come down from the top by way of easy ledges and gullies.

review.notes: Route page gives the location and the descent.

set.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. The route is the centre line of the second Dog's Tooth from the left, on the buttress between Infinite Jest and A-Frame. It begins by ascending a snowfield to clean cracks in the middle right of the buttress.
set.descent_text: Walk off the back, following game trails down to the meadows. The alternative is a series of double-rope rappels from the top of the fifth pitch down to the bottom of the snowfield.

review.notes: Route page: location and both descents. Rappel count left out.

set.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. The route climbs the steep northeast face of the Monolith, the large formation on the cirque.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. Walk straight from the lake to the foot of the line, which takes the prominent chimney and crack system straight up the middle of the largest formation in the cirque and leans left near the top.
set.descent_text: The summit is a surprisingly flat plateau. Walk down gentle, non-technical ground well to the east of the formation and back into the cirque.

review.notes: Route page gives the line and the walk-down east.

set.approach: The Mouth refers to a pair of limestone massifs where Clark's Fork Canyon opens out. From Cody go north on Wyoming Highway 120 to Clark, turn west at the Edelweiss Restaurant onto Canyon Road 1AB, trend left onto the road that follows to the canyon mouth, and walk a short way from the highway across a BLM fence to the routes. This line is the lower part of the route Forever.

review.notes: Mouth page: road access; route page: it is the lower part of Forever. No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the road into Clark's Fork Canyon and stop at a roadside pull-off on the right, near a fence gate. Head across toward the big slabs, bearing left. The route begins on top of a small rise, with a wash on its right, between two big trees; several bolts are visible from the ground.
set.descent_text: Rappel directly off the front of the summit spire to the walking ledge, scramble down to the anchors below, and rappel the route; some of the rappels can be skipped.

review.notes: Route page has the full approach and descent.

set.approach: Climb to the upper ledge system of High Plains Hoedown, walk right along the ledge until you can head up the massive gully system, and hike and scramble up it by the easiest line (if it becomes fifth class you have gone wrong) to the base of the large slab that sits left of a huge corner system capped with a tree ledge.
set.descent_text: Rappel back down the route, then scramble down and rappel High Plains Hoedown to finish.

review.notes: Route page gives approach and descent.

set.approach: The North Side Rock Climbs buttresses stand over the northern shore of Taminah Lake, in Avalanche Canyon. They are a short hike up from the lake, bearing left as you gain height so as to skirt the lower cliff band in between. The approach is only a little longer than the one to Irene's Arete.

review.notes: Crag page gives the hike; route page says the approach is modest. No descent detail stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the Death Canyon trailhead by the park's southern entrance, climb to the Phelps Lake overlook and descend into Death Canyon proper, then watch for the talus slope that climbs to Omega Buttress a few minutes after the second switchback. Hike the talus to a gully below the buttress, using fourth-class terrain on the right side, and continue up the loose gully to the base. The route climbs the southeast face of the Ship's Prow, left of Cardiac Arete and right of Edge of Horror, beginning at the right-hand end of the approach slab, the start all Ship's Prow lines use.
set.descent_text: Use the Omega Buttress descent: rappel from the large tree with many slings into the gully, downclimb a short step, follow the trail to skier's left (do not rappel from the furthest tree), make a short rappel to a dirty ledge, then follow a faint trail of third- and fourth-class ground back to the base of the buttress.

review.notes: Route page sends the descent to the buttress descent; buttress page describes it.

set.approach: Reach Omega Buttress from the Death Canyon trailhead: hike to the Phelps Lake overlook, descend into Death Canyon, and climb the talus and loose gully to the base of the buttress. Begin from a tree on a small grassy ledge a short way west of the standard slab start shared by all Ship's Prow routes, below the obvious crack.
set.descent_text: For a one-pitch outing, belay from the ledge, then scramble east to a large tree that can be used for the descent.

review.notes: Route page: start and the tree descent. Fixed anchor not assumed.

set.approach: The route is on the Sawtooth ridge right above Powder River Pass, the high point of Highway 16, so the walk to the base is short. It follows the steepest line up cracks and jug rails to the ridge, then continues north along the crest to the grass.
set.descent_text: From the crest, circle east around the talus to return to the pass, or retrace the ridge.

review.notes: Route page gives both.

set.approach: Ram's Head Buttress is in the northern Wind River Range, in the Green River area, beyond the second lake. The route is on the left panel of the buttress, starting at the bottom of the ridge feature to the right of that panel and following slabs, chimneys and broken ground up the ridge.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right of the buttress.

review.notes: Route page: start and walk-off.

set.approach: Roadside Cave is a south-facing limestone cliff just west of Trail Lake Road (County Road 411), above the inlet to Trail Lake. The route is on the far left wall, left of the main wall.
set.descent_text: After topping out, walk off to either side.

review.notes: Crag page: location; route page: walk-off either side.

set.approach: Leave the vehicle in the lot and take the trail beside the river down to a big rock; the outcrop of rock slabs is on the far side of the river, which means fording the river and then walking up to them.

review.notes: Crag page gives the access; route page has no location.

set.approach: Leave the vehicle in the lot and take the trail beside the river down to a big rock; the slabs are on the far side of the river, so you have to cross it and walk up. The top of the slab can be reached by walking around, which gives access to build a top-rope anchor from rocks.

review.notes: Crag page gives access; route page: top-rope slab reached by walking around.

set.approach: Hike the Death Canyon trail until you are opposite the face, using the Apocalypse Couloir and the large talus and snow cone below it as the guide. Cross the creek and work up the apex of the talus. Reaching the start of the pitched climbing is a significant effort in itself, through vegetated gullies and third- to low fifth-class ground up to where the vegetated gully feeding the waterfall tops out; immediately to the left of the final short steep section on dark rock, a left-trending crack and ramp system starts. The route follows the arete or prow left of Raven Crack, the major dihedral line in the centre of the wall.
set.descent_text: There are several options. Rappel the route using blocks, trees and one fixed anchor, rappel the wall to skier's right, or rappel Raven Crack, which has some fixed anchors. Walk-off options are the Son of Apocalypse Couloir or a lengthy hike eastward to the Open Canyon trail.

review.notes: Route page has approach and descent options; face page gives the creek crossing and talus. Counts left out.

set.approach: Springfield Gully is a short walk from the camp in the Cirque of the Towers, in the cuts of the buttress at the edge of camp, below the Watchtower. A climbers' path from the campsites runs under the gentle slabs on both sides; most of the routes here lie in the left-hand cut. Walk up the gully to a hidden wall on the south side, where Kamp Krusty is the largest continuous crack.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the gear anchor to climber's left, down the narrow gap beside the crack.

review.notes: Route page: location and rappel.

set.approach: Springfield Gully is a short walk from the camp in the Cirque of the Towers, in the cuts of the buttress at the edge of camp, below the Watchtower. Follow the gully's north side upward beyond a long slabby block; the route is on a small west-facing in-cut on the northern edge of the gully.
set.descent_text: Downclimb the short chimney when done.

review.notes: Route page: location and downclimb.

set.approach: St. Lawrence Basin is a remote group of cirques approached from the east, above the valley floor near Dubois. The route climbs the evident arete on Lightning Rod Spire.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route; all the anchors are bolted.

review.notes: Route page: arete and rappel. Basin page: approached from the east.

set.approach: St. Lawrence Basin is a remote group of cirques approached from the east, above the valley floor near Dubois. The route climbs a prominent spur jutting out from the west end of Saddle Mountain's north face.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the Dry Horse Creek trail up to a point even with the tower, then go up the mahogany-covered hillside to the tower's west end. The route starts in the dihedral just left of the west arete and finishes on the east arete.
set.descent_text: Rappel the southwest face to the ground.

review.notes: Route page: start/finish and southwest-face rappels; tower page: trail. Counts left out.

set.approach: Park at the Death Canyon trailhead and follow the Buck Mountain and Stuart Draw climbers' trail, which passes under Albright Peak and bends west into the draw. The climbs are on the south side, and you can see them from the draw's one large stream crossing; a good climbers' trail stays south of the creek but fades into forest and scree, so the last stretch is line-of-sight and some bushwhacking. The route is on the draw's south side, up the tallest and most conspicuous buttress of dark granite, starting in a vegetated corner that faces right, somewhat to the right of a lone bolt that has anchors above it.
set.descent_text: Descend the narrow gully or couloir directly west of the summit. The footing is loose, though it needs no technical skill, and it leads straight back to the foot of the climb.

review.notes: Route page: start and descent; draw page: approach.

set.approach: Sunrise Ridge continues Taminah Arete: from the top of Taminah Arete, descend with a rappel and a downclimb to the saddle on the north between Matternaught and Gilkey, then begin from the saddle's west side. Taminah Arete itself is reached by heading northwest from the lake's west end, going beneath the East Ridge buttress, and finding a weakness at the west end of the cliff band guarding its base.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit of Gilkey Tower. Descend Garnet Canyon by the South Teton trail.

review.notes: Route page: start and descent; arete page: approach to the arete.

set.approach: The Old Log Dam is the first wall in Warm Spring Canyon: take the trail from the parking lot beside the creek. The route is at the end of the main wall.

review.notes: Wall page: trail; route page: end of main wall. Descent wording too unclear to use.
